Find LCM by taking every required prime factor with the greatest exponents.

Use HCF(a,b) × LCM(a,b) = a × b for two positive integers.

Recognise and correct common HCF/LCM exponent mistakes.
Apply HCF/LCM to real-life grouping and repeated-event contexts.
Use prime factorisation confidently enough to support HCF/LCM reasoning.
Explain why HCF uses common minimum powers while LCM uses all required maximum powers.

concept_learning.title: Understand HCF & LCM Through Prime Factorisation

learning_sequence.title: 1. What is HCF (Highest Common Factor)?
learning_sequence.summary: The largest positive integer that divides all given numbers without leaving a remainder.

points.text: Definition: Greatest common divisor of integers a and b.
Factorisation Rule: Product of the smallest powers of each common prime factor.

learning_sequence.formula: HCF(a, b) = Product of smallest powers of common primes

learning_sequence.title: 2. What is LCM (Least Common Multiple)?
learning_sequence.summary: The smallest positive integer that is divisible by all given numbers.

points.text: Definition: Smallest common multiple of integers a and b.
Factorisation Rule: Product of the greatest powers of every prime factor involved.

learning_sequence.formula: LCM(a, b) = Product of greatest powers of all primes

learning_sequence.title: 3. The Two-Number Identity Bridge
learning_sequence.summary: Fundamental relationship connecting HCF and LCM for any two positive integers:

points.text: Use Case: Quickly find LCM when HCF is known: LCM = (a × b) / HCF.

learning_sequence.formula: HCF(a, b) × LCM(a, b) = a × b

points.text: HCF: Uses min(x, y) because a common factor cannot exceed what both numbers contain.
LCM: Uses max(x, y) because a common multiple must contain enough factors for both numbers.

learning_sequence.title: 5. HCF & LCM for 3 or More Numbers
learning_sequence.summary: Extending prime factorisation to 3, 4, or more numbers:

points.text: HCF(a, b, c): Smallest powers of primes common to ALL 3 numbers.
LCM(a, b, c): Greatest powers of EVERY prime appearing in ANY of the 3 numbers.

learning_sequence.title: 6. ⚠️ Critical Board Exam Rule: Identity Limitation
learning_sequence.summary: The product formula does NOT extend to 3 numbers!

points.text: HCF(a,b,c) × LCM(a,b,c) ≠ a × b × c in general.
Always calculate HCF and LCM for 3 numbers directly from prime factorisations.

learning_sequence.trap: Never use HCF × LCM = a × b × c for 3 numbers!

mnemonics.text: HCF → Common to all numbers + Minimum powers
LCM → All required primes present + Maximum powers
HCF × LCM = a × b (Strictly for 2 numbers only!)
